title: Principality of Lippe
capsule: Lippe was a small German principality in Westphalia, centred on Detmold, which joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1807 following the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire. After 1815 it was recognised as a sovereign state within the German Confederation, and a Landtag was established in 1836. A military convention of 1867 placed Lippe's forces under Prussian command within the 26th Infantry Brigade, effectively ending its independent military; in 1871 it became one of the constituent states of the German Empire, remaining formally sovereign until its abolition in the revolution of 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Borders and administrative structure are well documented through German imperial records; Lippe's territory was compact and changed little from 1806 to 1871.
